title: Isolating a phone: airplane mode and Faraday bags
quick: Isolation means stopping a seized phone from using mobile, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth networks, so new data or remote commands cannot change the evidence. Airplane mode and Faraday containers are common tools.

sections.title: Why isolate
text: A connected phone can receive messages and calls, sync apps and accept a remote wipe or lock command. Any of these can change or destroy evidence. Isolation reduces that risk.

sections.title: Airplane mode and Faraday containers
text: Airplane mode turns off radios, but it needs you to touch the phone, and some radios may still run or come back on. A Faraday bag or box is a shielded container that blocks radio signals. Guidance says shielding may not stop every signal, so test your container regularly. Cables passing through the shield can also act as antennas.
points: Airplane mode: changes the phone, must be checked.
Faraday container: no touch needed, needs testing.
Isolation card or other methods: can also be used.

sections.title: Power and battery
text: A phone inside a shield keeps searching for signal and the battery drains fast. If it turns off, it may need the passcode and access may be lost. Plan for power, using a method that does not break the shield, and follow your lab's procedure.

sections.title: Record what you do
text: Write down the time, the method and the state of the device before and after. Procedures and laws differ by country and agency.

example: A phone is found switched on and unlocked. The first officer places it in a tested shielded container with a power bank cable arranged by the lab procedure, and notes the time, the battery level and the network symbols shown on the screen.
mistakes: Believing a Faraday bag always works without testing it.
Switching airplane mode on a locked phone by guessing.
Breaking the shield to connect a cable and reconnecting the phone to the network.
Not writing down when isolation was done.

terms.meaning: A phone setting that turns off radio transmission.
A shielded bag or box that blocks radio waves.
A command sent over a network that erases a device.
Radio frequency signals used for mobile and wireless networks.

exam.q: Why is a Faraday bag tested before use?
exam.a: Some shields only reduce signals, so a test shows whether the phone can still connect.

exam.q: Why is airplane mode alone not always enough?
exam.a: It needs interaction with the phone, and some wireless functions may stay on or be turned back on.
